title: Automated KMS/Vault + TLS certificate rotation and secrets automation for Private installer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require repeatable, auditable automation for key management and TLS lifecycle to meet compliance and uptime SLAs. This PR adds an end-to-end installer path that provisions customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), integrates HashiCorp Vault as an optional transit layer, and automates TLS certificate issuance and rotation via cert-manager + sealed-secrets.

Summary of changes: Adds Terraform modules, Helm chart updates, and installer hooks so the operator can opt into: (1) provisioning an envelope encryption key in cloud KMS or configuring PKCS#11-backed HSM; (2) wiring that key to a Vault Transit backend (optional) for centralized signing/encryption; (3) configuring the sealed-secrets controller to use an external key provider; (4) automating certificate issuance and zero-downtime rotation for internal mTLS via cert-manager and Kubernetes deployment rolling semantics. The installer now accepts a single high-level config block: "kms_provider" with choices [aws_kms, gcp_kms, azure_keyvault, pkcs11_hsm, vault_transit]. The implementation uses envelope encryption for persistent secrets and short-lived signing keys for TLS.

What this PR touches (high level): Terraform: modules/tls_kms (new), modules/hsm_connector (new). Helm: charts/sealed-secrets/values.yaml, charts/redwood-core/values.yaml (cert-manager config), charts/installer/templates/hooks.yaml (pre/post-install hooks for key bootstrap). Installer CLI: cmd/install/main.go (new flags), pkg/installer/provisioning.go (k6 logic). Docs: docs/private/kms-and-tls.md and migration notes.

Design notes: - Default behavior remains unchanged for users who do not opt in. - When kms_provider=vault_transit we do not provision cloud KMS keys; instead we create a Vault role/secret-engine and store envelope keys in Vault with a TTL. Vault integration is pluggable: the installer writes a minimal policy and a long-lived management token into the control plane secrets that only the provisioner uses. - For HSMs we added a small PKCS#11 shim container that mounts credentials and exposes a gRPC adapter to the sealed-secrets controller. This keeps dependencies out of the controller binary. - Seal/unseal: existing sealed-secrets flow is preserved but the controller key is now optionally provided by the external KMS/HSM. We also add migration tooling that re-encrypts existing SealedSecrets with the new key in a deterministic, batched process to avoid cluster-wide restarts. - TLS rotation: cert-manager issues new certificates with overlapping validity and the rollout controller triggers a rolling restart of pods annotated with redwood.com/auto-rotate=true. We implement a two-phase rotation (prep + cutover) to ensure no simultaneous certificate expiry.

Security and compliance: - All provisioning calls are logged to the auditor (installer emits linear IDs and request IDs). - KMS keys are created with constrained key policies (minimum principals) and key-rotation metadata. - Secrets at rest remain envelope-encrypted; the private key material for TLS is never written to plain files on disk by the installer. - For HSM-backed setups we document FIPS and PCI considerations in docs.

Testing performed: - End-to-end in staging using AWS KMS + Vault Transit: created key, validated envelope encryption for persistent secrets, rotated controller key and observed zero-downtime SealedSecrets decryption. - HSM flow tested against SoftHSM and a PKCS#11 mock for functional parity. - Cert rotation exercised with canary clusters (50% rollout) and synthetic traffic to validate no TLS hiccups. - Unit tests: new installer package coverage 78%. Integration tests: terraform apply/destroy in CI smoke job.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge in main. 2) Publish new installer release candidate and smoke in internal staging. 3) Enable opt-in in a pilot customer cluster (support + SE present). 4) Promote to GA config once pilot confirms.

Rollback plan: the installer writes a migration log and a reversible mapping of old->new secret envelopes. If any issues occur we run the included migrate/revert tool to rewrap secrets with the previous key and restart sealed-secrets controller with previous config. HSM migrations are flagged as non-automatic (operator must confirm rollback).

Notes and caveats: - Vault integration requires network access and a managed auth path; we provide a bootstrap token but recommend switching to AppRole or IAM-based auth post-install. - PKCS#11 HSM setups require operator intervention for initial module installation and PKCS#11 library path; we document steps but cannot automate hardware plug-in. - This PR intentionally avoids changing the default key provider to avoid surprising existing customers.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform modules - [x] Helm chart changes - [x] Installer CLI flags and docs - [x] Migration tooling and tests - [x] E2E validation in staging

References: Linear ENG-3279 for automation spec; SEC-410 for security review.

release_notes: Automated support for customer-managed KMS/HSM, optional Vault Transit integration, and cert-manager-based TLS rotation for Private installer. Includes Terraform modules and Helm chart integration. Opt-in only; no default changes.
risk_assessment: Medium: introduces new external dependencies (Vault, HSM). Defaults unchanged and feature is opt-in; migration tooling reduces blast radius. Recommend pilot rollout before customer enablement.
